Booker's brother, [[Trevor Booker|Trevor]], also played college basketball at Clemson and played professionally in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Booker's cousin, [[Jordan Hill (basketball)|Jordan Hill]], is a former NBA player as well.[https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/wizards-insider/post/wizards-trevor-booker-still-waiting-to-play-his-cousin-jordan-hill/2012/01/27/gIQAkyzVWQ_blog.html Wizards’ Trevor Booker still waiting to play his cousin, Jordan Hill.] ==High school career== Booker played high school basketball at Union County High School, in [[Union, South Carolina]]. ==College career== After high school, Booker played [[college basketball]] at [[Clemson University]], with the [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson Tigers]], from 2009 to 2013. ==Professional career== Booker began his pro career in France, during the [[2013–14 LNB Pro A season]], with [[SLUC Nancy Basket|SLUC Nancy]]. Later that same year, he moved to the [[LNB Pro B|French 2nd Division]] club [[JL Bourg-en-Bresse|JL Bourg]]. He was named the [[LNB Pro B#LNB Pro B Finals Most Valuable Players|Finals MVP]] of the [[2013–14 LNB Pro B season]]. In 2015, he joined the [[LNB Pro A|French 1st Division]] club [[Élan Chalon]], where he also played in the [[FIBA Europe Cup]], where Chalon finished in third place. In the [[2015–16 LNB Pro A season]], Booker was named the league's [[LNB Pro A MVP|Most Valuable Player]].{{Cite web | url = https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Pro-a-devin-booker-mvp-vincent-collet-meilleur-coach/657235 | title = Pro A : Devin Booker MVP, Vincent Collet meilleur coach|work = [[L'Equipe]] | date = 29 April 2016}} In 2016, Booker agreed to join the [[New York Knicks]] for the [[NBA Summer League]]. On July 17, 2016, he signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga|BBL]] in Germany.{{cite news|title=Bayern Munich lands Devin Booker|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/206643/bayern-munich-lands-devin-booker.html|access-date=17 July 2016|date=17 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160720023755/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/206643/bayern-munich-lands-devin-booker.html|archive-date=20 July 2016|url-status=dead}} On July 12, 2017, Booker re-signed with Bayern for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=Bayern Munich re-signs Devin Booker|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/240901/bayern-munich-re-signs-devin-booker.html|access-date=12 July 2017|date=12 July 2017}} He averaged 12.4 points and 5 rebounds per game during the season. Booker re-signed with the team on July 17, 2018.{{Cite web |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/germany/bbl/282145/bayern-munich-re-signs-devin-booker.html |title=Bayern Munich re-signs Devin Booker |access-date=2018-07-17 |archive-date=2018-07-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180717184016/https://sportando.basketball/en/germany/bbl/282145/bayern-munich-re-signs-devin-booker.html |url-status=dead }} On July 16, 2019, Russian club [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] announced that they had signed Booker to a one-year deal.{{cite web|title=KHIMKI ADDS DEVIN BOOKER TO THE ROSTER|url=https://en.bckhimki.com/news/clubnews/2019/july/1431|date=16 July 2019|website=bckhimki.com|access-date=16 July 2019}} On July 5, 2020, Booker officially renewed his contract with the Russian club Khimki with an option for an additional year, which also competes in the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=DEVIN BOOKER STAYS IN KHIMKI TILL 2021|url=https://en.bckhimki.com/news/clubnews/2020/july/1545|date=5 July 2020|website=bckhimki.com|access-date=5 July 2020}} On June 16, 2021, Booker signed a two-year deal with [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] of the [[Basketball Super League|Turkish Basketball Super League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fenerbahce-signs-devin-booker-to-two-year-deal/|title=Fenerbahce signs Devin Booker to two-year deal|last=|first=|date=June 16, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 16, 2021 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} On July 24, 2023, Booker returned to Bayern Munich, penning a two-year contract. On July 15, 2025, Booker signed a multi-year contract with [[Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Devin Booker signs with a new team|url=https://basketnews.com/news-227311-devin-booker-officially-switches-teams.html|access-date=October 27, 2025|website=basketnews.com|language=en}} ==Personal life== Booker is the brother of
